title: Finite-width altermagnetic quantum rings: angular-channel hybridization and Aharonov--Bohm physics
abstract: We study a finite-width two-dimensional quantum ring with a quadratic $d$-wave altermagnetic term, Tan--Inkson confinement, a perpendicular magnetic field, and independently tunable Aharonov--Bohm (AB) flux. The altermagnetic interaction mixes $m$ and $m\pm2$ angular channels while preserving their parity. Circular symmetry renders the crystal orientation spectrally irrelevant and makes the two spin blocks exactly isospectral. The resulting same-parity anticrossings are resolved at low filling, and multichannel mixing is found near the Fermi level of highly occupied rings. Independent converged calculations for $N_e=1400$ and $1800$ establish the reconstructed Fermi edge and magnetic response in a finite field window and the persistent current over a full AB flux period. The analytic conventional reference separates radial-subband depopulation (dHvA-type cycles) from finer finite-ring shell oscillations; we do not assign a global Fourier spectrum to unverified altermagnetic field scans. The few-electron thermal response is obtained from an exact fixed-particle-number canonical partition function, avoiding finite-system errors of a fixed-mean-number approximation. The circular model supports an equilibrium charge current but no persistent spin current.
summary: This theoretical work examines how a d-wave altermagnetic interaction modifies the electronic spectrum and persistent current in a quantum ring under external magnetic fields. By analyzing angular channel hybridization, the authors demonstrate unique spectral features and confirm the existence of a charge current without a persistent spin current. This research is significant for understanding spin-charge coupling in artificial magnetic structures.
main_problem: The study investigates the spectral, magnetic, and persistent current properties of a finite-width quantum ring subjected to a quadratic d-wave altermagnetic term, a perpendicular magnetic field, and tunable Aharonov-Bohm flux.
main_result: The altermagnetic interaction mixes angular channels while preserving parity, leading to exactly isospectral spin blocks in the ideal circular model. The system supports an equilibrium charge current but no persistent spin current.
method: The analysis uses an effective-mass description solving the single-particle Hamiltonian, examining channel hybridization and comparing results to known phenomena like dHvA oscillations.
model_or_system: The system is a finite-width, 2D quantum ring in an altermagnetic material, modeled by a Hamiltonian combining the Tan–Inkson confinement potential and the d-wave altermagnetic term. The study intentionally omits electron-electron interactions and SOC.
key_observables: Spectral changes (anticrossings, Fermi edge reconstruction), magnetic response, and persistent current over a full AB flux period.
important_parameters: The dimensionless altermagnetic coupling parameter ($ eta$) and the Aharonov-Bohm flux ($\Phi_{AB}$), as well as the perpendicular magnetic field ($B$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the single-particle level, and the perfect circular geometry is assumed for key symmetry results.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general Hamiltonian incorporating the altermagnetic term, analyzes the hybridization of angular channels, and calculates key observables like the persistent current and magnetic response under varying magnetic fluxes.
why_interesting: The combination of magnetic field control (AB flux) with intrinsic magnetic order (altermagnetism) in a mesoscopic geometry provides a rich platform for studying topological and spin-related quantum effects, bridging condensed matter magnetism and quantum confinement physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Low-energy Aharonov–Bohm spectrum for κ = 4.5 and B = 0. (a) Conventional Tan–Inkson ring, β = 0. (b) Altermagnetic ring with β = 0.20. Blue solid and orange dashed curves denote the even- and odd-m parity sectors, respectively. Crossings between channels connected by ∆m = ±2 are converted into anticrossings, whereas crossings between opposite angular- parity sectors remain symmetry protected. Panels (c) and (d), obtained from a 401-point local scan over −0.06 ≤ϕAB ≤0.06, resolve the two smaller same-parity gaps at ϕAB = 0: 1.533 × 10−3ℏω0 in the even sector and 1.564 × 10−3ℏω0 in the odd sector. Energies are shown in units of ℏω0.

FIG. 2. Near-Fermi spectral reconstruction at κ = 50 and ϕAB = 0.25. Panels (a) and (b) show representative ∆m = 2 crossings for Ne = 1400 and 1800 at weak altermagnetic coupling β = 0.005. The conventional bare branches, the projected 2×2 model, the full-spectrum spectral weight, and adiabatically tracked branches are shown together. Panels (c) and (d) display the corresponding full spectra at β = 0.20, where the selected pair is embedded in a dense manifold, and the response becomes strongly multilevel. The plotted energy is measured relative to the local mean of the selected bare pair, ¯Epair(b) = [E(0) n,m(b) + E(0) n,m+2(b)]/2; at b = bc this reference coincides with the bare crossing...

FIG. 3. Zero-temperature persistent charge current for Ne = 4, κ = 4.5, and B = 0. The conventional Tan–Inkson open shell has a zero-flux current discontinuity. The altermagnetic m = −1 ↔+1 anticrossing removes the cusp in the many- body energy and converts the jump into a continuous flux response.

FIG. 4. Many-electron conventional Tan–Inkson benchmark at κ = 50, ϕAB = 0, and T = 0. Panels (a) and (b) show the Fermi edge for Ne = 1400 and 1800, respectively, determined from the Heaviside particle-number constraint. Panels (c) and (d) show the exact orbital magnetization from Eq. (111), normalized per electron. Vertical dashed lines mark the successive depopulation of the highest occupied radial subband. The large oscillatory cycles track these depopulation events, whereas the finer structure at lower field is produced by discrete angular-level rearrangements within an unchanged set of radial subbands.

Figure 5 shows the Fermi edge and the local magnetic response alongside the exact β = 0 Tan–Inkson reference. The two many-body energy series (β = 0 and 0.20) are differentiated with the same five-point local polynomial stencil on the ∆b = 0.001 grid, avoiding artificial differ- ences introduced by comparing a smoothed curve to an unfiltered derivative. Since the spectrum exhibits rapid occupation rearrangements, the plotted magnetization represents a finite-grid response estimate: at a cusp it averages nearby one-sided slopes and should not be inter- preted as the unique pointwise derivative. Away from a cusp, the expectation-value form of the derivative is pro- vided by Hellmann–Feynman...
